function: Receiver beamforming and device selection for over-the-air gradient aggregation in FL, solved by optimization (SCA, greedy, alternating) to minimize a training-loss bound (p. 1, 6, 7).
system: Uplink over-the-air FL: server with N=16 antennas, M=200 single-antenna devices; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 4, 9).
method: Federated learning (FedSGD) of logistic regression (MNIST) and ResNet-14 (CIFAR-10); the PHY design is optimization (SCA, greedy GSDS, alternating ADSBF), not learned (p. 3, 9, 11).
data_channel: Own simulator: complex Gaussian channels with COST Hata path loss, 200 devices at 10-100 m, constant during training; MNIST and CIFAR-10 for the learning task (p. 9).
test_conditions: Single configuration: M=200 devices, N=16 antennas, static channels; results averaged over 20 channel and noise realizations; MNIST noise -20 dBm, CIFAR-10 -50 dBm (p. 9, 10, 11).
baselines: Select all and Top one (paper-defined heuristics); Gibbs sampling [22] and DC programming [20], earlier published joint beamforming and device-selection designs (p. 9).
metrics: Average test accuracy and test loss with 95% confidence intervals over 20 realizations, number of selected devices, and design run time (p. 10, 11).
complexity: GSDS O(M^3), ADSBF O(M log M), Gibbs and DC O(M^4) for M >> N (p. 9); MNIST run time: GSDS 585.7 s, ADSBF 8.1 s (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 9: "The path loss follows the COST Hata model"; the channel is complex Gaussian CN(0, I/PL), a custom simulator with no COST 2100, 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "over the 20 different channel realizations" of one setting (M=200, N=16, p. 9); no other number of devices, antennas, or channel is tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "DC approach [20]" and "Gibbs sampling [22]" are earlier published designs, with "Select all" and "Top one" as simple baselines; p. 10: "which is 15% higher than the best accuracy achieved by the benchmarks".
q4_support: p. 8: "The computational complexity of the proposed GSDS grows" with the number of devices as O(M^3); Table 2 (p. 9) gives O(M log M) for ADSBF; Table 3 (p. 11) gives run times.
q5_support: p. 9: "The simulation codes are available online at" https://github.com/faezemoradik/BeamformingDeviceSelecetionDesignInFLwithOTA (footnote 2).
notes: Passes the learning check under the FL rule: the learned element is the FL model, while beamforming and device selection come from optimization (p. 6, 7, 8). Path loss is COST Hata, not COST 2100, so the reviewer may confirm q1. q3 applies the FL rule, with [20] and [22] as earlier published designs. Tables 2 and 3 were read from page images.
